author: FantasyPoints Staff
key_reason: Hurts has a new playcaller in Sean Mannion, who comes from a McVay-LaFleur background. The new scheme will feature more under-center plays and play-action, which historically boosts Hurts' efficiency. Additionally, his legs are expected to be a key part of the wide-zone running scheme, and the offensive line is projected to bounce back from injuries.
upside_metric: Never dipped below 21.7 FPG from 2021-24, and has been significantly better in YPA (8.76 vs 7.44) under center than in shotgun since 2021.
risk_factor: Coming off his worst fantasy season under Kevin Patullo, posting career-lows in rushing attempts (6.6) and rushing YPG (26.3).

author: FantasyPoints Staff
key_reason: Prescott is a great value compared to Joe Burrow, going multiple rounds later. He led all passers in attempts, completions, and passing yards per game when playing full games last season, and the Cowboys' offense is expected to remain highly productive with a high implied team total.
upside_metric: Ranks third in completions/game (23.9), second in TD passes/game (1.96), and first in end-zone targets/game (2.73) since returning from his 2020 leg injury.
risk_factor: Averages just 11.4 rushing YPG since his leg injury, limiting his ceiling to challenge for the absolute top FPG spot at the position.

author: FantasyPoints Staff
key_reason: Lawrence is in the best situation of his career, entering his second season under Liam Coen, who has a history of coaxing career-high passing touchdowns from his quarterbacks. The Jaguars' offense is expected to remain pass-heavy with an improved receiving corps including Jakobi Meyers.
upside_metric: Turned in 20 total TDs and 23.7 FPG (QB1) in his final nine games of the season, and won fantasy championships in Weeks 15-17 as the QB1 with 33.2 FPG.
risk_factor: Rushing production is expected to regress after posting career-highs in yards (359), TDs (9), and FPG (5.3) last season.

author: FantasyPoints Staff
key_reason: Purdy was a league-winner when healthy last season and is in an even better position now that the 49ers have added Mike Evans in free agency, giving him a premier perimeter and downfield threat to counter defenses that take away the middle of the field.
upside_metric: Finished as the QB5 with 21.0 FPG, including a massive 32.3 FPG (QB2) in the fantasy playoffs (Weeks 15-17), and owns an elite 6.2% TD rate through four seasons.
risk_factor: Missed eight games due to a severe turf toe injury last season, and showed vulnerability in games where defenses successfully took away the middle of the field.

author: FantasyPoints Staff
key_reason: Willis secured a massive contract from the Dolphins and possesses elite dual-threat rushing ability. If he secures a starting job, his rushing upside makes him a high-ceiling option despite playing in a potentially weak offense.
upside_metric: Scored 52.2 FP on just 47 dropbacks last season, averaging an incredible 1.11 FP/DB when on the field.
risk_factor: His rushing style can hurt the fantasy outlook of his skill players, and Miami's lack of offensive talent gives him a very low floor.

author: FantasyPoints Staff
key_reason: Murray has the opportunity to revive his career under Kevin O'Connell in Minnesota, whose pass-heavy offense ranks in the top six in passing yards and pass rate over expectation.
upside_metric: Possesses top-five upside when in the lineup due to his career average of 36.7 rushing YPG, and previously averaged 19.1 FPG to finish as the QB9 under O'Connell.
risk_factor: Not guaranteed to start the entire season, especially if his play struggles like it did last year, and must win an open competition in training camp.

author: FantasyPoints Staff
key_reason: Shough showed legitimate potential as a 26-year-old rookie once he took over the starting job in Week 8, demonstrating strong fantasy viability down the stretch.
upside_metric: Reached 17.1+ FP and 239+ passing yards in seven of his final eight starts, ranking as the QB9 (18.8 FPG) from Week 10 through the end of the season.
risk_factor: Failed to win the starting job to begin his rookie season, and faces a weak receiving corps behind star wideout Chris Olave.

author: FantasyPoints Staff
key_reason: The Eagles are undergoing massive offensive changes under Sean Mannion, who brings a Sean McVay/Matt LaFleur background. Barkley noted the new system will feature more under-center and outside zone concepts, which will help him see the field better and run downhill quicker behind a top-5 offensive line.
upside_metric: Averaged 3.09 YBC/ATT and 4.92 YPC with a 15% explosive run rate on 108 under-center runs last season.
risk_factor: Expected regression from his monster 2024 campaign, though the market has overcorrected.

author: FantasyPoints Staff
key_reason: The Jets extended Hall with $29 million guaranteed, signaling bell-cow usage. Geno Smith's addition should raise the floor of the offense, helping Hall push for a top-12 finish in a more efficient scoring environment.
upside_metric: Jets scored touchdowns on just 14.4% of their drives last season, leaving massive room for positive regression.
risk_factor: Braelon Allen's presence as a high-quality backup and potential workload-sharer.

author: FantasyPoints Staff
key_reason: Skattebo quickly climbed to the top of New York's depth chart last season. He has a chance to replicate his rookie success in a much better offensive environment, especially with a healthy Malik Nabers keeping defenses honest.
upside_metric: Averaged a healthy 18.6 FPG in the six games he played more than half of the snaps, which would have made him the RB6 overall.
risk_factor: Recovering from a major right ankle dislocation, fibula fracture, and deltoid ligament rupture.

author: FantasyPoints Staff
key_reason: Houston has big plans for Montgomery as their new lead back following Joe Mixon's departure. He is a safe bet to post RB2 production based on volume alone, with top-12 upside in a high-scoring offense.
upside_metric: Averaged 4.2 YPC or better in each of his last three seasons, including 4.53 YPC last year.
risk_factor: Houston's offensive line ranked 30th in adjusted YBC/ATT (1.45) and 30th in success rate (45.1%) last season.

author: FantasyPoints Staff
key_reason: Tuten gets the first crack at replacing Travis Etienne in one of the NFL's best offenses. He has league-winning upside if he can relegate Chris Rodriguez to a limited role and maintain pass-catching duties.
upside_metric: Finished with the highest success rate (57.8%) among rookie RBs since 2021.
risk_factor: Potential three-man committee with Chris Rodriguez and pass-catching specialist LeQuint Allen.

author: FantasyPoints Staff
key_reason: Swift is one of the safest RB2 bets in fantasy, never finishing lower than RB25 in his career. He has a solid floor behind a strong offensive line and possesses bell-cow potential if his backfield mates miss time.
upside_metric: Finished 10th in YPC (4.87) and 5th in explosive run rate (15.1%) last season.
risk_factor: The emergence of rookie Kyle Monangai could turn the backfield into a two-man committee.

author: FantasyPoints Staff
key_reason: Stevenson is a proven veteran available three rounds cheaper than his sophomore teammate TreVeyon Henderson, despite outperforming Henderson in almost every key rushing and receiving metric last season.
upside_metric: Bettered Henderson in explosive run rate (13% vs 11.1%), YAC/ATT (2.75 vs 1.91), and YP_RR (1.41 vs 0.98).
risk_factor: Henderson taking a significant step forward in his second year, causing the coaching staff to flip their roles.

author: FantasyPoints Staff
key_reason: Gainwell quickly earned the trust of Aaron Rodgers to become the clear #2 option in the passing game. He offers weekly standalone value due to his high-volume receiving profile and massive contingency upside.
upside_metric: Finished 4th among RBs in receptions (73), 5th in receiving yards (486), and 5th in YAC (526) last season.
risk_factor: Tampa Bay's backfield could devolve into a three-man committee with Bucky Irving and Sean Tucker.

author: FantasyPoints Staff
key_reason: White has the inside track to handle passing-down snaps and is the best bet to earn a fantasy-relevant role in this backfield, offering low-end RB2 potential if he secures a near bell-cow role.
upside_metric: Caught at least 40+ passes in each of his four seasons and posted his best success rate (53.8%) last season.
risk_factor: He is a finesse runner who doesn't create many big plays, ranking 41st in runs of 15+ yards (3%) last season, and the backfield could become a fantasy nightmare.

author: FantasyPoints Staff
key_reason: Carolina passed on adding a back in free agency and the draft, leaving Brooks with a clear path to take over the backfield from a declining Chuba Hubbard if he is healthy.
upside_metric: Could potentially win fantasy leagues if he's completely healthy and takes over the Panthers backfield.
risk_factor: He has appeared in just three games since November 2023 due to a pair of torn ACLs in the same knee, making him highly risky if drafted inside the top-100 picks.

author: FantasyPoints Staff
key_reason: Locked in as the #1 receiver for Patrick Mahomes in a highly pass-heavy offense, offering elite upside if he can avoid further off-field trouble.
upside_metric: Finished as the WR6 with 18.8 FPG after serving a six-game suspension last season, ranking 5th in TPRR (.31) and 16th in YPRR (2.28).
risk_factor: Offseason legal issues, including a jail sentence and probation violation, mean he could face suspension or trouble at any time.

author: FantasyPoints Staff
key_reason: Higgins is a dominant perimeter option who will challenge for the league lead in receiving touchdowns with better injury luck in a high-powered passing offense.
upside_metric: Scored 21 times on 200 targets (9.5%) and 924 routes (2.3%) over the last two seasons, outperforming Chase on a per-target and per-route basis in TDs.
risk_factor: Missed seven games over the last two seasons and is coming off five-year lows in YPRR (1.71) and TPRR (.19).

author: FantasyPoints Staff
key_reason: Flowers is the clear #1 target for Lamar Jackson with Mark Andrews declining and secondary options like Isaiah Likely and DeAndre Hopkins departing.
upside_metric: Has seen his target share (27.7% > 24.1% > 22.7%), air yards share (35.1% > 30% > 23.7%), and receiving yards (1211 > 1059 > 858) rise in each of his first three seasons.
risk_factor: Plays in a run-heavy Baltimore offense that averaged a league-low pass rate of 53.4% and just 27.3 attempts per game.

author: FantasyPoints Staff
key_reason: Set to be the clear top option for the first time since his rookie season following A.J. Brown's trade to the Patriots, with potential to push for top-5 WR status.
upside_metric: Averaged 6.7 receptions, 79.7 yards, and 9.7 targets per game (16.6 FPG) in three non-Week 18 contests without A.J. Brown over the last two seasons.
risk_factor: Adjusting to a new offensive system under coordinator Klint Kubiak.

author: FantasyPoints Staff
key_reason: Now playing under Sean McVay with the Rams, Adams remains an elite red-zone weapon who will be heavily targeted in scoring areas.
upside_metric: Averaged a ridiculous 1.93 end-zone targets per game last season and owns the most total end-zone targets (76) in the Fantasy Points Data era.
risk_factor: He is the clear #2 wide receiver behind Puka Nacua and is coming off a 10-year low in receiving yards per game (52.6).

author: FantasyPoints Staff
key_reason: A premier big-play threat in a potent Detroit offense that has the NFL's easiest schedule, coming off back-to-back 1000-yard seasons.
upside_metric: Ranked third in YPR (17.22) and fourth in YPT (11.21) over the last two seasons.
risk_factor: Prone to disappearing at times, totaling just 5.7 FP with two goose eggs over his final 12 games last season, and needs to clean up drops.

author: FantasyPoints Staff
key_reason: Primed for a bounce-back season in David Blough's new offense with a healthy Jayden Daniels and no significant target competition.
upside_metric: Will benefit from a more versatile route tree after running an NFL-high 81.6% of his routes from the left side of the line of scrimmage last season.
risk_factor: Fell from WR15 production (15.8 FPG) to WR34 production (11.4 FPG) last season while dealing with a quad injury.

author: FantasyPoints Staff
key_reason: Evans joined a new team for the first time at 33 years old, opting for an upgrade at playcaller (Kyle Shanahan) and quarterback (Brock Purdy). He remains a matchup nightmare and a beast as an end-zone threat.
upside_metric: Purdy owns an elite 6.2% TD rate through four seasons, and Evans has scored on 7.2% of his career targets.
risk_factor: Age (33 years old) and recent hamstring and collarbone injuries that slowed him down over the last two seasons.

author: FantasyPoints Staff
key_reason: Watson is poised to easily clear his career-best 68% route share after the Packers thinned out their WR corps by letting Romeo Doubs walk and trading Dontayvion Wicks.
upside_metric: Watson averages 17.5 FPG across 13 career games above a 75% route share.
risk_factor: Injury history, specifically missing the first seven games of last season to recover from an ACL injury.

author: FantasyPoints Staff
key_reason: Washington showed the most fantasy potential at the end of last season, with Trevor Lawrence leaning heavily on him in the biggest games of the year.
upside_metric: Averaged 3.23 YPRR with a 32.1% target share when all three WRs were on the field at the same time.
risk_factor: More downside than BTJ and Meyers because he is the most likely to lose routes when the Jaguars use 12 personnel.

author: FantasyPoints Staff
key_reason: The Chargers brought in Mike McDaniel to call plays, which could unlock Johnston's after-the-catch ability. The team also showed faith by exercising his fifth-year extension.
upside_metric: Averaged the second-most YAC/REC (8.9) in college football in 2022.
risk_factor: Johnston has been a boom-or-bust weekly option to start his career and has mostly been a frustrating fantasy asset.

author: FantasyPoints Staff
key_reason: Pittman has a chance to bounce back in his first season away from Indy, pairing perfectly with Aaron Rodgers who has an incredibly fast release time.
upside_metric: Rodgers' teams have ranked top-12 in pass rate inside the 10-yard line in three of his last four seasons.
risk_factor: Coming off his worst receiving YPG (46.1) since his rookie season and must compete with D.K. Metcalf for targets.

author: FantasyPoints Staff
key_reason: Robinson posted his first 1000-yard season with Malik Nabers missing the final 13 games, showing off his speed as a downfield receiver with a deeper aDOT.
upside_metric: Averaged 2.23 YPRR against zone coverage compared to 1.50 YPRR against man.
risk_factor: Robinson is a small receiver (5'8", 185 pounds) and there is mild concern with the NFL moving away from 11 personnel.

author: FantasyPoints Staff
key_reason: Downs will finally play in more 2-WR sets after the Colts decided to move forward with Alec Pierce as the #1 WR over Michael Pittman.
upside_metric: Averaged 13.0 FPG in the 11 games he's been above a 75% route share.
risk_factor: He has never been a target magnet through three seasons, coming off career-highs in target share of only 17.4%.

author: FantasyPoints Staff
key_reason: Warren will take on a bigger role in the passing game after the Colts decided to pay Alec Pierce and trade away Michael Pittman.
upside_metric: Ranked as the TE5 in expected FPG (11.7), which was the second largest negative difference (-.6) in FPG and expected FPG behind T.J. Hockenson.
risk_factor: Finished as one of the worst separators at the position, ranking 37th out of 40 TEs in Average Separation Score.

author: FantasyPoints Staff
key_reason: Kraft carried Green Bay's passing game through the first seven games before a torn ACL ended his season prematurely.
upside_metric: Tied with Trey McBride as the TE1 with 16.2 FPG through the first eight weeks.
risk_factor: Recovering from a torn ACL suffered in Week 9.

author: FantasyPoints Staff
key_reason: LaPorta is the cheapest way to get access to Detroit's high-powered offense (third-highest implied team total) with massive upside if Amon-Ra St. Brown or Jameson Williams misses time.
upside_metric: Averaged 15.9 FPG in 18 career games reaching his route participation threshold, with career-highs in YPRR (2.14) and catch rate (81.6%).
risk_factor: His third season was cut short after nine games because of a herniated disc, which required surgery.

author: FantasyPoints Staff
key_reason: Kelce still maintains a significant role in a passing game led by Rashee Rice, offering serviceable low-end TE1 volume with touchdown upside.
upside_metric: Led the Chiefs in targets (108), receptions (76), and receiving yards (851) at 36 years old.
risk_factor: His efficiency continued to dip, averaging 1.67 YPRR and .21 TPRR on a 74% route share.

author: FantasyPoints Staff
key_reason: Goedert is a massive winner from the A.J. Brown trade, expected to see an uptick in target share and first-read share in the middle of the field under the new offense.
upside_metric: Averages 5.4 targets/game, 53.4 receiving YPG, and 12.3 FPG in seven games without A.J. Brown in the lineup.
risk_factor: Goedert will face touchdown regression after scoring an unsustainable 11 TDs in 15 games last season.

author: FantasyPoints Staff
key_reason: Andrews has a clear path to more consistent targets as the clear #2 receiver behind Zay Flowers in an offense ranking sixth in implied team total.
upside_metric: Finished in the top eight at the position in end-zone targets in every season during the Fantasy Points Data era.
risk_factor: Coming off career-lows in receiving yards (422) and YPR (8.8) in his eighth season, combined with Baltimore's low-volume passing offense.

author: FantasyPoints Staff
key_reason: Likely joined the Giants in free agency to be the lead tight end ahead of Theo Johnson, slotting in as the #2 receiver for Jaxson Dart behind Malik Nabers.
upside_metric: Ranked as the TE5 in FPG (13.9) in Weeks 12-18 when given the starting opportunity previously.
risk_factor: Suffered a foot fracture at the start of training camp in his final season with the Ravens, which contributed to a career-low 21.9 receiving YPG.
